newsitem.title: UKRAINE: NEW UKRAINE MINISTER EXPLAINS GRAIN MOVEMENT BAN.
newsitem.headline: NEW UKRAINE MINISTER EXPLAINS GRAIN MOVEMENT BAN.

text.p: Ukraine's new agriculture minister on Thursday explained why some of republic's regions barred commercial companies from obtaining grain until state orders are filled.
Yuri Karasyk said Khlib Ukraina, the state grain concern, was concerned about claiming its grain since it was worried about it rotting in fields and silos after heavy rains.
He added the government would also talk to the regions not releasing grain.
"There will not be a lot of this happening in Ukraine," said Karasyk, who took over last month at the renamed ministry for the agro-industrial complex.
Local and foreign companies are angry because state-owned elevators and farms in at least half of Ukraine's 26 regions are not releasing pre-purchased grain, which also happened last year.
Karasyk said the regions were aware commercial businesses would have to be paid ahead of the 1998 harvest.
The minister said 1.2 million tonnes had been claimed for the state purchase order, set at 5.88 million tonnes this year against 5.00 million in 1996.

An official at the U.S.-funded Citizens' Network group, set up to promote private business in the mostly state-run sector, said on Wednesday the government was pressing farms to pay back years of debts, preferably in grain.
"The farms are interested in giving their grain to state orders or they won't get new resources," Karasyk said. "They cannot only pay commercial businesses."
He added Ukraine would do away with state orders in 1998.
Ukraine has forecast a grain harvest of 37-38 million tonnes this year against 25.4 million tonnes in 1996.
